officeActionSection112Text:
claims 1-12 are rejected under 35 u.s.c. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which applicant regards as the invention.
in claim 1, line 3, “the pattern of illumination” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 1, line 6, “the horizontal direction” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 1, line 6, “the vertical” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 1, line 6, “the first lens” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 1, line 7, “the received light” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 2, lines 3-4, “the other end” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 2, line 5, “the light emitted by the led light sources” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 3, line 5, “the spread pattern” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 3, lines 5-6, the superimposition lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 4, line 3, “the respective arrays” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 4, line 4, “the respective array” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 4, line 7, “the first lens” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 4, line 9, “the light projected” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 7, line 1, “the optical coupling” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 7, lines 1-2, “the each respective one end” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 12, line 3, “the other end” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 12, lines 3-4, “the general shape” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 12, line 5, “the ends lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 12, lines 5-6, the fiber optic cables” lacks antecedent basis.
in claim 12, line 6, “the desired illumination beam pattern” lacks antecedent basis.
claims recite numerous limitations with insufficient antecedent basis. the claims are replete with such errors and each claim should be checked to insure that they particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter the applicant regards as his invention.
